channel.title: Nicotine Science and Policy
channel.description: Daily digest of views, debates and discussions on nicotine science, policy, regulation and advocacy.

item.title: Malaysia's Alarming Vape Ban
item.description: Malaysia’s vape ban debate should raise concern for anyone focused on outcomes rather than appearances. Removing legal access to lower-risk products can push consumers towards illicit supply, reduce oversight and leave adult smokers with cigarettes as the more stable option. Youth protection deserves strong enforcement, but broad bans often weaken the very safeguards they claim to create. A better approach would regulate vaping responsibly while keeping the route away from combustion open. (Published on September 22, 2026byplanetofthevapes.co.uk)

item.title: Australia’s 5.8% Smoking Rate: Accurate, Misleading, or Both?
item.description: A smoking rate is only as reliable as the data behind it. Australia’s 5.8% figure raises questions about what is being counted, what may be missed and how illicit tobacco use affects the picture. A low number can shape policy confidence, media narratives and international reputation, so the methods matter. Before Australia is held up as a success story, its smoking data needs to match the reality of the market. (Published on September 22, 2026bysubstack.com)

item.title: FactFind: Are vapes 'nearly worse' than cigarettes?
item.description: The phrase “vaping is worse than smoking” does more than misstate the evidence — it changes behaviour. A smoker who believes that message may see little reason to switch, even though cigarettes remain the far more harmful product. Good fact-checking restores the missing hierarchy: vaping is not harmless, but it is not smoking. Clear risk communication can be the difference between staying with combustion and taking a less harmful route away from it. (Published on September 22, 2026bythejournal.ie)

item.title: Youth vaping has collapsed, but lawmakers want $500 million to fight it anyway
item.description: Half a billion dollars to fight a collapsing trend deserves scrutiny. Youth vaping has fallen sharply, yet lawmakers are still treating it as an expanding emergency while adult smoking remains the bigger driver of preventable disease. Resources should follow the scale of harm, not the politics of alarm. Serious nicotine policy would protect young people without using outdated crisis language to justify measures that may also make quitting harder for adults. (Published on September 22, 2026byreason.org)
